sections.h2: Which routes get a Haverstraw house sold fastest?
sections.html:
In the Town of Haverstraw the quickest exit is a deal with a cash purchaser who accepts the property in its present condition, since an agent listing or a private sale both wait on showings, financing and appraisals. Owners with a house in good order and no deadline can still do better on price by listing.

Haverstraw lies in Rockland County along the Hudson River, and the town includes the Village of Haverstraw along with hamlets such as Garnerville, Johnsontown, Ladentown, Mount Ivy and Samsondale. Sellers here deal with a town assessor, a town Receiver of Taxes whose penalty calendar is short, a town Building Department, and the Rockland County Clerk for the deed.

  • Agent listing: the usual path when the property is in good order.
  • Owner sale: keeps the fee, but you handle disclosure and contract work.
  • Cash sale: built for probate homes, houses needing work, or owners facing tax penalties.

sections.h2: How big and how costly is Haverstraw, per the Census?
sections.html:
QuickFacts gives Haverstraw 40,462 residents for July 2025, up from 39,087 in the 2020 count, a gain of about 1,400. Among homes, 64.8% are owner-occupied, and their median value for 2020 to 2024 is $387,500.

Rent runs a median $1,906. The town has 12,366 households of 3.11 people on average, the largest household size among the four towns in this batch, and median household income is $89,107 in 2024 dollars. Commuters spend a mean 30.1 minutes getting to work, and just over a third of adults (34.1%) finished a bachelor's degree. On 22.15 square miles of land, density was about 1,765 people per square mile when the 2020 census was taken.

sections.h2: How is the Town of Haverstraw laid out?
sections.html:
The town covers 27.41 square miles, but 5.26 of them are water, and it stretches across Rockland County's northern section from the Hudson River to the western county line. The village of Haverstraw holds the historic downtown, and part of Harriman State Park, including Lake Sebago, Lake Welch and Lake Kanawauke, lies in the west of the town.

Settlers took the name from the Dutch Haverstroo, oat straw, which described the riverside grasslands; a land purchase from local natives in 1666 was confirmed as a patent in 1671. The town was formed in 1788 and later gave up land for Clarkstown and Ramapo in 1791 and Stony Point in 1865. A calico printing plant built in 1828, a complex of some 30 buildings in Garnerville, now operates as the Garnerville Arts and Industrial Center.

  • Roads: the Palisades Interstate Parkway, US 9W, US 202 and NY 45.
  • Ferry: the Haverstraw to Ossining crossing of the Hudson, tied to Metro-North.
  • Bus: Short Line coaches run along US 9W toward Port Authority Bus Terminal.
  • Parks: Bowline Point Town Park and the Long Path trail.

About a fifth of the town's area is water, so a parcel near the river or a lake deserves a look at its drainage and flood history before you pick an asking price.

The Haverstraw-Stony Point Central School District is the one the Town of Haverstraw names in its tax collection notice, with parcels inside it eligible for installment payment of school tax. Under that arrangement, at least 50% is due by September 30, a second installment of at least half the balance by October 13, and the remainder before November 3.

Look at your bill for the district name and the installment option, since a buyer will ask what the school line shows.

sections.h2: How does Haverstraw assess property, and what are the dates?
sections.html:
The Town Assessor assigns a dollar value to every parcel, vacant or improved, residential or commercial, and that value feeds town, county and school tax. The office also handles exemption applications and the STAR program and helps defend grievances, small claims assessment review and certiorari cases.

Haverstraw assessment calendar (source: Town of Haverstraw Assessor's Office)
DateStep
July 1, prior yearValuation day
March 1Taxable status day
May 1Tentative roll filed
4th Tuesday in MayGrievance Day before the Board of Assessment Review
July 1Final roll published

For 2026 the grievance filing window ran from May 1 to May 28 and has closed, so the next chance comes with the 2027 tentative roll. The office provides a printable grievance application and a questionnaire for proposed assessments, so gather them before May.

sections.h2: What penalties apply to late Haverstraw tax payments?
sections.html:
Town and county tax is collected from January 1 through January 31 without penalty, and the Town of Haverstraw, a town of the first class, adds 1% in February and 2% in March. On April 1, unpaid tax is turned over to Rockland County Finance.

  • Installments: bills above $50 may be paid in four parts, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31.
  • Later parts: April 15, July 15 and October 15, paid to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance in Pomona.
  • March payments: after March 15, checks must be bank or certified checks, in the office by close of business on March 31, with no postmarks accepted.
  • Cards: accepted, with a 2.45% convenience fee charged by the card provider.

Elderly or disabled owner-occupants of one-, two- or three-family homes can ask the Receiver of Taxes for third-party notification on form RP-923. A seller closing mid-year should ask the closing attorney which installment has been paid, so the proration comes out right.

sections.h2: What permits should a Haverstraw seller check?
sections.html:
The town Building Department issues building permits and Certificates of Occupancy and points owners to section 84-4 of the Town Code to see which repairs and construction need them. Those documents show that a house meets the codes for structural soundness and fire safety.

Before you list, confirm that every addition, finished basement and converted space has a permit and a Certificate of Occupancy on file. The department also handles questions about fire permits, burning permits, fire inspections and sprinkler systems.

sections.h2: How do the deed and transfer tax work for a Haverstraw sale?
sections.html:
Haverstraw deeds go to the Rockland County Clerk, whose land records page requires originals in recordable form, legible, signed and notarized. State transfer tax runs $2 per $500 of the price, rounded up, so the $387,500 Census median value would owe $1,550, usually from the seller.

The state tax return and payment are due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered, and the clerk takes them when the deed is recorded. A buyer owes a 1% mansion tax on a residence at $1 million or more. The clerk's land records page offers downloadable forms for the most common filings.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Haverstraw taxes after March?
faqs.a: Rockland County Finance takes over collection of unpaid bills on April 1. Until then the Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and late-March checks must be certified or bank checks.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 grievance deadline still open in Haverstraw?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 filing window ran from May 1 through May 28. Grievance Day falls on the fourth Tuesday in May each year, so the next chance is spring 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay Haverstraw taxes in installments if I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if the bill is over $50, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31. Later parts fall on April 15, July 15 and October 15, so ask your attorney which have been paid before closing.

faqs.q: Which authority records a Haverstraw deed?
faqs.a: The Rockland County Clerk, which accepts only original, legible, signed and notarized documents. The transfer tax return goes in within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: Will a buyer ask for a Certificate of Occupancy in Haverstraw?
faqs.a: The town Building Department issues them to show a building meets code, and a buyer's attorney may ask for one covering an addition or conversion. Section 84-4 of the Town Code lists which work needs permits, and the department can answer questions.
